text.en:
Every morning a truck came to collect rubbish in Rahul's city. One day it did not come, and the smell spread.
His father called the ward councillor, and by evening the truck was back.
"The city's local government looks after these things," he said.

Local government in towns and cities is called urban local government. In big cities it is a Municipal Corporation. In smaller towns it is a Municipality (Nagar Palika), and in small urban areas a Nagar Panchayat.
A city is divided into wards. People of each ward elect a councillor. The councillors together form the council. The Mayor heads a Municipal Corporation.
Municipalities look after water supply, roads, street lights, drains, rubbish collection, public toilets, parks and markets. They also give birth and death certificates.
They get money from taxes such as house tax and water charges, and from the government.
Elections are held every five years. Citizens can tell their councillor about problems in their ward.
In towns and cities, local government is the municipality. Big cities have a Municipal Corporation.
A city has wards. Each ward elects a councillor.
A Mayor heads a Municipal Corporation.
The municipality looks after water, roads, lights and rubbish.

problem.en: Who should you tell if the street light in your ward is not working?

text.en: Street lights are looked after by the municipality.
Each ward has an elected councillor.

why.en: The councillor listens to ward problems.

text.en: So tell the ward councillor or the municipal office.

prompt.en: A friend says the city's rubbish is not the government's job. What will you say?

requiredIdeas.en: The municipality is the local government and rubbish collection is one of its main jobs.
We should also keep the city clean by not littering.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking only people should keep the city clean.

points.en: Urban local bodies: Municipal Corporation, Municipality, Nagar Panchayat.
Each ward elects a councillor; a Mayor heads a corporation.
They look after water, roads, lights and rubbish.
